title: Release Train: Sprint Zero Stabilization Notes (WIP)
content:
Meeting: Release-Train Sprint Zero stabilization sync
Date: 2026-03-10 10:00 PT
Attendees: Marissa (owner), Ethan, Aisha, Olivia, Tom, +observability on call (ad-hoc)
TL;DR: Quick sync to capture stabilization checklist for sprint-zero release train. We accepted two new gating rules (prefix-KV cache warmup and quantized-model smoke tests) and agreed a 48h hotfix SLA window for P0 regressions during the 2-week ramp. This doc is WIP — will convert to playbook after two more dry-run deploys.

Agenda:
- Current signals and thresholds for automated rollback
- Hotfix intake and triage workflow (who, where, when)
- Canary schedule and ramp percentages for model variants (q4/q8/float16)
- Capacity forecast block for Dedicated pools during ramp
- Open questions / blockers

Summary of decisions:
1) Automated rollback triggers: any sustained increase >2x baseline error-rate for 5 minutes OR p95 latency > 2x baseline for 10 minutes triggers a soft rollback (canary -> baseline) and PagerDuty P1 escalation if persists 10 minutes after rollback.
2) Hotfix SLA: P0 (customer-facing data corruption, eviction) = 4h initial ack, 48h resolution target during ramp; P1 = 8h ack, 72h resolution target. Documented in REL-7842.
3) Canary roll schedule: 0% -> 1% after 15m smoke -> 5% after 30m -> 20% after 1h -> 50% after 4h -> 100% after 24h if all signals green. Must pass quantized-model smoke tests at 1% and 5% gates.
4) Cache warmup policy: prefix-KV prefill period = 10 minutes post-canary-start; if cold-miss rate > 25% relative to baseline, hold ramp and triage.
5) Dedicated capacity bump: reserve +1.5x burst capacity (GPUs) for first 48h of ramp; ops to pre-warm node pools by 2:00 AM UTC before deploy day.

Hotfix triage matrix (working table):
- Severity / Example / Intake channel / Owner (first contact) / Target ACK
- P0 / user data loss or training-tokens-corruption / #release-ops + PD / Marissa / 4h
- P1 / severe latency regression causing user timeouts / #release-ops + oncall / Ethan / 8h
- P2 / minor accuracy drift / email + ticket / Olivia / 24h
- P3 / cosmetic logs / ticket / Tom / 72h

Runbook snippets (short checklist - to be forked into CLI-runbook):
- Pre-deploy (T-2h): verify canary infra green (k8s nodes Ready, autoscaler not saturated), confirm dedicated burst pool pre-warmed, confirm metrics dashboards live (p95, p99, error-rate, token-failure-rate).
- Canary start: tag canary with release id, start routing rule (1% -> 5% as schedule), enable KV-cache prefill endpoint (/internal/cache/prefill?release=<id>). Watch for warmup-drop in cache-hit; if >25% miss => pause.
- On rollback: flip routing to baseline via feature-config, notify #release-ops with rollback tag, attach last 15 minutes of trace logs to the incident, run postmortem stub.

Telemetry & dashboards to watch (links sent in Slack during deploy):
- latency-p95/model-service (per-model)
- token-failure-rate (total and per-region)
- kv-cache-hit-rate (prefix and global)
- ingress-error-rate (4xx/5xx split)
- GPU-utilization and queue-depth for Dedicated pools

Capacity notes (numbers are approximate and to be validated with infra):
- Baseline: 1200 concurrent token streams across hosted API in us-west1 during peak.
- Expected spike during ramp: +18% CPU load and +22% token throughput until cache warms.
- Dedicated bump requested: add 6 A100 nodes (or equivalent) for 48 hours. Ops to confirm procurement/quotas by 2026-03-12.

Open action items (owner / due):
- Create automated smoke checks for q8 quantized path (Ethan / 2026-03-12)
- Add KV-cache prefill endpoint to infra runbook and permission matrix (Tom / 2026-03-11)
- Validate Dedicated burst quota with cloud accounts (Aisha / 2026-03-12)
- Draft post-deploy annotation template for change logs (Marissa / 2026-03-13)
- Wire up small-run chaos test for canary latency variance (Olivia / 2026-03-18)

Open questions & risks:
- Q: If the quantized model exhibits subtle output drift at 20% traffic, do we fallback to float16 globally or only on affected routes? (Decision: prefer route-level fallback where possible; otherwise global fallback. Need runbook examples.)
- Risk: Cloud provider preemption window overlaps with canary window next Thursday — must verify node preemption SLAs and schedule non-critical workloads off the pool.
- Risk: Observability retention currently 7d for detailed traces; need 14d for postmortem of ramp issues. Ops ticketed.

Notes to self / meeting scribbles (informal):
- Folks asked whether we should add an experiment tag for model-variant in the logs to make A/B aggregation easier — agreed, prefix logs with tag:release.sprint0.variant.<q8|q4|float16>.
- Ethan championed a 'soft' canary rollback first (reduce percentage) before full routing flip; need to document criteria in runbook.
- Put a sticky on follow-up: run a rehearsal with full pager rotation next Tue at 03:00 UTC (low traffic).

Next steps:
- Convert this doc into Playbook (Confluence) after two successful dry-run deploys (expected by 2026-03-18).
- Follow up owners will update tickets listed in linked_artifacts and close action items in sprint planning.

Appendix (quick links):
- REL-7842 (hotfix SLA), CORE-1310 (canary rollback automation), GH PR 912 (kv prefill endpoint), #release-ops (live channel)

Endnotes: keep this doc as the canonical sprint-zero stabilization notes until playbook merges. If you update, add an edit note with date and initials.
